summary: Materialized and read Railton Moral Realism pp. 201–204: he retains moral obligation even where a rational agent lacks an instrumental reason, explicitly judges Hitler morally ought not to have killed six million Jews (p. 203 n. 41), and rejects categorical rational compulsion. Rejected inferring moral permission or absence of obligation from absence of a categorical reason. This specific example does not establish an exceptionless prohibition of all innocent nonthreatening killing or sexual violation, nor a categorical reason for an indifferent agent. Precise source scope and remaining application gaps are in docs/naturalistic-moral-realism.md, Hard-case research section.
